verdict.rationale: Dynadot's own docs say it offers DNS and that its API can programmatically manage DNS, so DNS hosting exists as a first-party capability. Nothing in the evidence covers the specifics of the story: which record types are supported, minimum TTLs, or what the web management UI is like. Missing for 10: documented list of supported record types, low-TTL support, evidence of a developer-friendly DNS management UI, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, full DNS hosting comes with the domain — every record type, low TTLs, and a management UI that doesn't fight me

citations.quote: The Dynadot API lets you programmatically manage domains, account settings, DNS, orders, and other account activities.
Dynadot is an ICANN-accredited domain registrar offering domain registration, aftermarket services, DNS
